title: DiffusionGemma Technical Report
blurb: Google released DiffusionGemma, an experimental open-weight model that uses discrete diffusion to generate text in parallel blocks of 256 tokens rather than one token at a time. Fine-tuned from the Gemma 4 mixture-of-experts model on under 10% of its original token budget, it reaches roughly 1,500 output tokens per second on a single H100 while retaining thinking mode, multimodal inputs, and long-context support.

title: Don't be a meat proxy
blurb: The author argues that pasting an AI's verbatim output into Slack, code reviews, or group chats adds no value, since anyone can query the model themselves faster and with better context. Real contribution comes from reading, validating, and rewriting the response in your own words, which serves as proof you actually did the work rather than acting as a "meat proxy" between the reader and the model.

title: Don't be a meat proxy
blurb: The author argues against acting as a "meat proxy," relaying AI output verbatim in Slack threads, pull request feedback, or code review instead of engaging directly. Pasting a raw Claude response adds no value, since the recipient could query the model themselves with better context control. The real contribution is reading, understanding, and validating the output, then responding in your own words as evidence that you did that work.

title: Don't be a meat proxy
blurb: The author argues that pasting an LLM's raw output into Slack, PR reviews, or group chats adds no value, since anyone can query the model themselves and control their own context. He contends the actual work is reading, understanding, and validating the output, then rewriting it in your own words, so acting as a "meat proxy" that relays verbose, jargon-dense, often plausibly wrong text just shifts the effort onto the reader.

title: Russia moves to restrict retail crypto trading to bitcoin, ether and USDT
blurb: Russia's central bank will restrict retail crypto trading to bitcoin, ether, and USDT on regulated exchanges starting September 1, capping non-qualified investors at 300,000 rubles (approx. $3,600) of purchases per intermediary annually while exempting qualified investors. The per-intermediary structure lets traders exceed that ceiling across multiple brokers, and crypto payments inside Russia remain prohibited under the July legislation these rules build on.
